name: Cercis

project_scope.selection_mode: Genus backfill from five source-pool names, resolved against existing canonical concepts
project_scope.note: Variety names are synonyms of corresponding installed subspecies. C. canadensis is a broader parent species concept, not a newly installed third subspecies. Do not create duplicate species from index count.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: On a leafy twig, check alternate, single, palmately veined heart-shaped to kidney-shaped leaves (NOT pinnately compound); then find flat, thin legumes with a narrow longitudinal wing at one suture. On flowering wood, look for pink pea-like blossoms often borne directly from old stems before leaf emergence. For texensis vs mexicana, examine hairs on *new branchlets and flower stalks* before trusting wavy leaf margins.
shared_traits: Deciduous shrubs or small trees with alternate simple cordate/reniform leaves, entire margins and palmate veins arising near the blade base.
Spring clusters of bilateral pealike flowers may appear on older leafless wood; ten stamens mostly free rather than the usual nine-plus-one papilionoid arrangement.
Dry flattened pods with a narrow wing along one seam; mature pod and venation separate from superficially similar woody plants.
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Fruit and twig structure confirm Cercis. Native-range evidence for a subspecies is a separate scientific decision; genus identity does not confer target-zone PASS.

species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. texensis: Generally glabrous or almost hairless on young twigs and flower stalks in traditional Texas treatments
species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. mexicana: Young twigs/pedicels characteristically woolly or pubescent in traditional treatments; degree varies
species_comparison_matrix.weight: BEST STRUCTURAL TIE-BREAKER; assess with macro and repeat on multiple shoots

species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. texensis: Thick/leathery, usually glossy above; often glaucous beneath
species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. mexicana: Also thick/leathery, often glossy and glaucous; substantial overlap

species_comparison_matrix.weight: SUPPORTING, not a reliable exclusive split

species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. texensis: Broad orbicular- to reniform-cordate, rounded or sometimes acute tip
species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. mexicana: Cordate-ovate to reniform, often rounded tip; wide continuous overlap

species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. texensis: Dry Texas limestone woodland, canyon and bluff sites; already canonical target-native in this project
species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. mexicana: More western xeric/Texas Trans-Pecos and Mexico association; canonical nonlocal comparison in this project
species_comparison_matrix.weight: CONTEXT ONLY; planted trees do not certify a wild range

species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. texensis: Pink pealike flowers and flat legumes; broadly shared by both
species_comparison_matrix.C. canadensis subsp. mexicana: Pink pealike flowers and flat legumes; broadly shared by both

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: single alternate blade, its palmate veins and a mature flat pod
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Confirm Cercis genus before attempting variety/subspecies; pod attachment and wing seam help distinguish from other legumes.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: several young branchlets plus flower pedicels in side macro
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Mostly hairless supports texensis; conspicuous woolly/pubescence supports mexicana in traditional identification. Degree and distribution may overlap.
Pronounced wavy margin leans mexicana; flatter leans texensis. Record texture, sheen, margins and blade tip but do not split solely by leaf waviness.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: provenance, geography, flowering versus leafy season
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Older flowering-only photos often cannot safely separate the two; keep Cercis canadensis complex until leaves and new shoots are documented.

overlap_and_cautions: Leaf size, tip shape, margin waviness and branchlet hairiness form a geographic and morphological gradient; a morphometric study of 281 specimens found continuous leaf variation and overlap between categories. Avoid a falsely perfect dichotomous key.
Floral photographs taken before leaves emerge are often insufficient to distinguish mexicana and texensis.
The canonical mexicana learner entry is non-target-zone LOOKALIKE_COMPARISON and must not be promoted to project-native merely because both are redbuds.
The parent C. canadensis record and both var. aliases are NOT three more installed species. The Sheet index counts source names, not accepted independent organisms.
Do not infer local native status from ornamental or cultivar specimens; document site provenance.

local_lookalike_routing.separate: Often thinner, duller ovate/cordate foliage with an acute tip compared with tougher glossier dry-country forms, but leaf variation overlaps; taxonomy and provenance needed.
Bilobed leaf tips may superficially resemble broad redbud foliage; inspect leaf architecture, flowers and fruit.
Overlapping rounded leaves and xeric habit; verify accepted concept and western provenance before assigning a name.

local_lookalike_routing.lookalike: other simple-leaved Fabaceae and heart-leaf ornamentals
local_lookalike_routing.separate: Require alternate palmate venation plus flattened one-carpel legume and redbud cauliflorous flowering pattern.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: pubescence versus near-glabrous twig, fresh nonworn tissue, shared scale and matched angle; label hair density as variable
blade front, dorsal face and edge-on undulation; same scale; never treat waviness alone as proof
old-wood flowering position, growth habit and leaf size at comparable maturity
pod attachment, flattened body, narrow suture wing, cross-section when possible
sepals, five petals, bilateral structure, ten free stamens; contrast with ordinary 9+1 papilionoid flowers
flowchart with source aliases → two accepted subspecies, and parent species remains broader concept

handoffs.question: Do not invent a morphological hard cutoff. Resolve ambiguous hairs/leaf variation by field provenance and review of Fritsch et al. 2009.
Ensure Master Plant Pool parent/var source names map to existing canonical concepts or documented broad species-level reference, without duplicate cards.

Lock same-scale young twig pubescence, stalk pubescence and edge-on leaf margin images; exact-species licensed photos with attribution/rights. Existing gallery state not claimed complete by genus text.
